_comment: Project layer (priority 2 of 4) for open-code-review, read by
.github/workflows/code-review.yml. The action checks out the TRUSTED
BASE, so a pull request cannot widen its own excludes.
`exclude` filters PER FILE, which the workflow's paths-ignore cannot:
paths-ignore skips a run only when EVERY changed file matches, so one
edited .txt beside 300 course records would send all 301 to the model.
That is what answered HTTP 413 and then retried into 429s. Both layers
stay: paths-ignore means a data-only pull request starts no runner at
all, and this means a MIXED one still reviews only the code.
What is excluded is generated or record data, which is not what an LLM
reviewer is good for: a course record is checked against the source URL
cited in the pull request body, and sync-data.mjs fails the build on a
bad mapName or an unknown venue.
Check any pattern with `ocr rules check <path>`, and check a whole diff
with `ocr review --preview --from main --to <branch>`, which prints the
verdict per file (user_exclude, unsupported_ext, ...) and calls no LLM.

rules.rule: This code reads SUTD's HTML, which changes without notice. Flag any parser that would write a THIN or EMPTY result over good data rather than refusing: a source answering 200 with nothing must never wipe a file. Flag file reads and writes that omit encoding="utf-8" - the repo's JSON is UTF-8 and the default on Windows is cp1252, which crashes before the scraper fetches anything.

Flag `continue-on-error` at JOB level where a later job gates on `needs.<job>.result`: it rewrites the result to 'success' on failure and silently disables the fallback. Step level plus a job output reading `steps.<id>.outcome` is the working form. Flag any push to main that does not authenticate as a token with the admin role, because main's ruleset requires a reviewed pull request and only that role bypasses it.

TypeScript strict, no `any` (use `unknown`). Comments must say WHY or HOW, never restate WHAT the line does. Flag anything adding analytics, tracking, cookies, telemetry, or a runtime dependency: all four are architecture invariants in CLAUDE.md. Flag a callback prop reaching an effect's dependency array where the effect builds an iframe or a subscription - an inline arrow is a new function every render and rebuilds it in a loop.
